memory_candidates.content: When a nix-flake-check quiet-host gate is needed on a shared multi-agent development machine, judge contention by load average (via uptime/proc/loadavg vs nproc), not by raw process count from `ps aux | grep -c <tool>`. Many idle background agent-CLI processes (waiting on I/O or user input) can inflate a process count to 40+ while CPU-active load stays well under the core count -- load average is the metric that actually predicts Z3-solve wall-clock contention and should be the deciding signal for whether a timing-sensitive test run is valid quiet-host evidence.

Wheel/sdist builds via python -m build are not byte-reproducible on this project's toolchain: independent rebuilds of the identical source tree produce different sha256 hashes each time (confirmed across three separate builds of the same commit during one task). When a rehearsal runner records sha256sums as evidence, document this explicitly so a future reader does not mistake hash divergence between rebuilds for a content regression -- the hash identifies a specific evidence run, not a fixed target value.
